title: answer_envelope.v1
description: One reply from the conversation layer. VERSIONED IN ITS FILENAME: v2 is a new file, never an edit to this one, because a stored message is rendered again months later and a schema edited in place would silently re-interpret it. FAILED is a transport outcome and is never rendered as a refusal.

status.description: ANSWERED: every engaged body answered. PARTIAL: some answered, some not held. NEEDS_LAWYER: a person must decide. ABSTAINED: we read and declined to answer. NEEDS_CLARIFICATION: intake could not tell what was asked. FAILED: the attempt broke -- TRANSPORT ONLY, never a statement about the law.

task.description: The task intake named. NEEDS_CLARIFICATION appears here too, because the envelope must be able to say 'no task was chosen' without inventing one. DRAFT was ADDED to this enum rather than starting a v2: widening an enum does not re-interpret any stored envelope -- every v1 envelope still validates and still means what it meant -- which is the failure the version-in-the-filename rule exists to prevent. A change that altered the MEANING of a stored field would require v2. Once a client ships against v1, even a widening becomes v2, because an old reader would meet a task name it does not know.

as_of.description: The date the law was read as at. Always present: an answer with no date is an answer about no particular law.

status.description: ANSWERED: obligations decided against held text. NOT_HELD: declared, and the refusal is named. CURRENT_ONLY: today's text held, no history, so no dated answer. NEED_FACT: engaged, and a fact is missing before it can even be classified. NOT_ENGAGED: considered and not engaged.

quote.description: The verbatim span. A citation whose quote does not byte-match its source is DROPPED before it reaches here -- see gateway/envelope.py.

state.description: CANNOT_READ must carry a reason. 'We could not read this page' and 'this document says nothing' are different answers and must never render the same.
